angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 406,845 km at 197.60 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0608 +/- 0.0214 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 197.60 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.5848 +/- 0.0026 solar radii from Jordán et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HATS-75 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..125J/abstract): 406,845 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.6017 +/- 0.0074 solar masses from Jordán et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HATS-75 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..125J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3790.4 +/- 5.7 K from Jordán et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HATS-75 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..125J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jordán et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HATS-75 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..125J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hats-75.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.683, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
